newsitem.title: USA: Volcker Commission making key decisions next week.
newsitem.headline: Volcker Commission making key decisions next week.

text.p: The commission headed by former U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Paul Volcker is poised to make major decisions next week affecting its probe into the unclaimed assets of Holocaust victims still in Swiss banks, sources close to the commission said on Thursday.

The sources said the commission, set up last year by the World Jewish Restitution Organisation (WJRO) and Swiss banks, is expected to name the first banks whose records will be audited in a pilot study that will precede an investigative audit of virtually every bank in Switzerland.
The first banks to be audited will include some of Switzerland's biggest, along with regional ones, the sources said.
They added that the commission will also discuss plans for a quasi-judicial procedure to resolve and accept claims for discovered dormant accounts in Swiss banks.
Jewish groups charge that millions -- perhaps billions of dollars -- are lying unclaimed in Swiss banks from Jews who sought a safehaven for their funds during the Second World War.
The commission is also expected to decide that the names on the dormant accounts should be made public, the sources said. This is not now possible because of Swiss bank secrecy laws.

The Volcker commission is meeting next Monday in Jerusalem at the same time as the executive board of the WJRO meets there to decide the criteria on a separate nearly $200 million fund set up by Swiss banks to aid needy Holocaust victims.
The WJRO is a branch of the World Jewish Congress.
